item.dc:creator: SI Reporter
item.content:encoded: Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates, Friday, Nov 6, 2026: The benchmark indices advanced as IT shares rose amid unwinding of global AI-trade. As of 10 AM, the Sensex fell 497.95 points or 0.63 per cent to 79,807.96, and the Nifty50 was up 87.90 points or 0.36 per cent at 24,623.75.  Hindalco Industries, Shriram Finance, and Asian Paints were the top losers in the Nifty50.  In the broader markets, the Nifty MidCap 100 and the Nifty SmallCap 100 fell 0.93 per cent and 1.54 per cent, respectively.  Sector-wise, the Nifty IT rose 1 per cent as unwinding of bets on global AI-linked shares boosted sentiment for domestic shares. The index was outperforming its peers. Meanwhile, Nifty Metal, Nifty Realty, Nifty PSU Bank, and Nifty Oil and Gas underperformed.   Q2 Results Today 3M India, AJAX Engineering, The Anup Engineering, Aster DM Quality Care, Azad Engineering, Blue Dart Express, Bluspring Enterprises, Bombay Dyeing & Manufacturing Company, Bosch, AvenuesAI, Cholamandalam Financial Holdings, Cohance Lifesciences, Data Patterns (India), Dynamatic Technologies, Elgi Equipments, Gland Pharma, Godrej Agrovet, Hindalco Industries, Hindustan Oil Exploration Company, Honasa Consumer, Ingersoll-Rand (India), Jubilant FoodWorks, Kirloskar Industries, Nuvama Wealth Management, Precision Wires India, Prism Johnson, Rain Industries, Ratnamani Metals & Tubes, Repco Home Finance, Rossell Techsys, Scoda Tubes, Siemens, Sirca Paints India, Star Cement, Supriya Lifescience, TTK Prestige, Voltas, Vardhman Textiles will release their results on Friday.

Home / Industry / Auto / Auto dealers warn high inventories, financing costs may hit demand

Auto dealers warn high inventories, financing costs may hit demand Passenger vehicle inventory stood at 43-45 days despite record wholesale dispatches, FADA said, while expressing hope that strong festive-season retail sales would help reduce stock levels

Passenger vehicle inventory remained at about 43-45 days despite record wholesale dispatches

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 06 2026 | 10:57 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Indian auto dealers warned on Friday that high inventories, rising financing costs and signs of rural stress could threaten post-festive demand despite record industry sales, with November retail sales key to clearing excess stock.   While automakers have reported strong wholesale sales, dealers say the focus is shifting to whether retail demand can sustain growth beyond the festive season.   Fada said October retail sales were hit by a delayed festive calendar, with passenger vehicle registrations falling 14 per cent from a year earlier and two-wheeler sales declining 28 per cent.   "The inventory today is not a major concern, but if it remains at these levels by the end of December, it becomes a major concern because dealers start losing money," Sai Giridhar, president of Fada, told Reuters.     Passenger vehicle inventory remained at 43-45 days in October, above the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations' recommended 21-day level. Also Read

Hyundai Motor India Q2 profit falls 23.9% as raw material costs rise

Car inventory levels lower this festival season amid rising demand premium

Renault CEO sees strong hybrids matching CNG's market share in India premium

Stellantis to invest ₹4,000 crore, launch 12 products in 3 years

BS-VII clock starts ticking as Centre sets 2029 target for emission norms

Giridhar said dealers were already seeing demand soften in some rural pockets affected by deficient rainfall, particularly in the two-wheeler segment, though he expects purchases delayed by the later festive season to support November sales.   Moreover, about 31 per cent of dealers reported a moderate or material impact from higher financing costs and loan repayments, while repeated vehicle price increases had eroded much of the benefit from last year's tax cuts, Fada said.   "If inventory continues at around 45 days, it will put pressure on dealers and OEMs to give extra discounts and liquidate inventory," Giridhar said.   Fada's comments follow robust October wholesales, including a record monthly sales figures for industry leader Maruti Suzuki, though analysts said part of the growth reflected inventory build-up at dealerships ahead of the festive season.

item.title: RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure
item.description: The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Banking / RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure

RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.

The Reserve Bank of India has proposed revised priority sector lending norms, including a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure and higher eligibility limits for education and renewable energy loans. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 11:16 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Reserve Bank on Thursday proposed that loans for agricultural infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system. As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions, the Reserve Bank of India said it has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue directions on the subject for different regulated entities, including commercial banks and regional rural banks. A draft direction on commercial banks proposed an aggregate loan limit of Rs 4 crore per borrowing entity for crop loans, medium and long-term loans for agriculture and allied activities, as well as loans for pre- and post-harvest activities.   It also said: "Loans for agriculture infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system."   The lending to the agriculture sector will include farm credit (agriculture and allied activities), lending for agriculture infrastructure and ancillary activities. The draft further said that loans to individuals for educational purposes, including vocational courses, not exceeding Rs 25 lakh, will be considered as eligible for priority sector classification. Also Read

RBI tightens cyber oversight of non-bank payment system operators

Ten years after note ban, how India's cash habit survived the UPI boom

RBI forms panel for consultation on financial markets, emerging risks

RBI forms financial markets consultative panel headed by Dy Guv Rohit Jain

Regarding renewable energy, it said bank loans up to a limit of Rs 35 crore to borrowers for renewable energy-based power generators and for renewable energy-based public utilities -- street lighting systems, remote village electrification -- will be eligible for priority sector classification. For individual households, the loan limit will be Rs 10 lakh per borrower, the draft said. Agriculture, MSMEs, exports, education, housing, social infrastructure, and renewable energy are among the categories under the priority sector. The RBI has also issued separate draft directions for small finance banks, local area banks, and regional rural banks. RBI has invited comments and feedback on the drafts by November 26.

item.title: Coal gasification can save ₹1.5 trillion in forex in 5-7 years: Coal secy
item.description: The Centre has committed financial incentives of ₹46,000 crore under two schemes to encourage coal gasification projects, said Coal Ministry Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / News / Coal gasification can save ₹1.5 trillion in forex in 5-7 years: Coal secy

Coal gasification can save ₹1.5 trillion in forex in 5-7 years: Coal secy The Centre has committed financial incentives of ₹46,000 crore under two schemes to encourage coal gasification projects, said Coal Ministry Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt

Coal gasification projects require substantial upfront capital investment as well as support at the state level in terms of electricity, water supply and taxation | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Panaji 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 2:26 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Coal gasification projects have the potential to save India around ₹1.5 trillion in foreign exchange over the next five to seven years through import substitution, Coal Ministry Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt said on Thursday. The Centre has committed financial incentives of ₹46,000 crore under two schemes to encourage coal gasification projects, Dutt said, addressing the 4th Conference of Mining Ministers on Reforms in the Mines and Coal Sector in South Goa. "Mining with a conscience" should be the guiding principle for responsible miners, the official added. He said coal gasification, which converts coal into synthetic gas (syngas), can help manufacture several products that India currently imports in substantial quantities.   "If the coal gasification projects get underway and gain scale, we would be succeeding in about five to seven years in saving about Rs one and a half trillion potentially of foreign exchange through this import substitution," Dutt said. Also Read

Govt asks coal miners to triple stockpiles to avert summer blackouts

Coal India files DRHP to sell 10% stake in subsidiary SECL through IPO

Captive, commercial coal production rises 42% to 22.03 MT in October

Coal imports by imported fuel-based power plants increase marginally in Aug

Partially explored coal mines to get upfront payment waiver benefit

"Coal gasification has the potential of becoming an instrument of industrial diversification and regional development," the official said, urging coal-producing states to introduce supportive policies to attract investments in the sector. Methanol, ethanol, and ammonium nitrate used in explosives and inputs for direct reduced iron (DRI)-based steel production could be manufactured through coal gasification, he noted. Odisha and Maharashtra have already introduced incentive policies to promote coal gasification, with projects coming up in clusters in Odisha's Angul district and Maharashtra's Chandrapur belt, Dutt pointed out. He also called upon coal-rich states such as Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Odisha to formulate policies offering incentives to investors, saying this would help attract projects and ensure that the benefits of central government schemes reach resource-rich regions. Coal gasification projects require substantial upfront capital investment as well as support at the state level in terms of electricity, water supply and taxation. Maharashtra and Odisha have taken steps in this direction, he said. Emphasising the employment potential of the sector, Dutt said gasification plants would generate jobs in downstream industries and benefit skilled and semi-skilled workers, besides strengthening local supply chains and creating additional economic activity. On coal sector reforms, Dutt said the commercial mining policy introduced in 2020 removed restrictions on end-use and sale of coal, paving the way for greater private participation. He said 137 mines had been allocated through 15 rounds of auctions, with captive and commercial mines accounting for around 20 per cent of India's total coal production. The government has also expanded the number of agencies authorised to undertake mineral exploration from 13 government agencies to 57, including 44 accredited private agencies, he informed. Dutt urged state governments to expedite land acquisition, public hearings, statutory clearances and other permissions required for operationalising coal blocks, saying delays in these processes often hinder mining projects. Faster operationalisation of auctioned coal blocks would ensure that states receive royalty and other revenue streams earlier, enabling them to fund development programmes, he stressed. Highlighting environmental initiatives, Dutt said the Coal Ministry had identified 147 mines for scientific closure over three years, of which 43 had already been scientifically closed. Scientific mine closure was not merely about technically sealing mines but also restoring degraded environments and repurposing mining areas after assessing the needs of local communities, he noted. The ministry has developed a digital tool called 'SuVikalp' to facilitate the assessment and repurposing of closed mines, he added. Dutt also stressed that the future of the coal sector should go beyond production targets and focus on productivity, technological advancement, transparency and environmental responsibility. "Mining with a conscience" should be the guiding principle for responsible miners, he said. The official also called for greater coordination between the Centre, state governments, coal companies and other stakeholders to make the sector competitive, efficient and environmentally sustainable. Union Minister for Coal and Mines G Kishan Reddy, MoS for Mines Satish Chandra Dubey and Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant were present on the occasion.
